title: UK Student Visa Application: CAS, Documents and Financial Evidence
seoTitle: UK Student Visa: CAS, Documents and Financial Evidence
seoDescription: Organise a UK Student visa application around your CAS, financial evidence and required documents, then check your decision and conditions.
primaryKeyword: uk student visa application step by step
intro: Your offer letter is only one part of a Student visa application. Check your CAS, financial evidence and required documents before submitting, using the current rules for your circumstances.
description:
Your offer letter is only one part of a Student visa application. Check your CAS, financial evidence and required documents before submitting, using the current rules for your circumstances.

Start with your offer and CAS

Follow your university's instructions for accepting the offer and obtaining a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies, known as a CAS. Check the course dates, personal details and fee information. If something is incorrect, ask the university to resolve it before you submit the visa application.

GOV.UK explains the Student visa route and the timing for applications made inside or outside the UK. Your circumstances determine which application process and supporting documents apply. An admission offer alone is not permission to enter or study in the country.

Check the financial evidence

Use the current GOV.UK financial requirements and the amounts on your CAS. The required course-fee evidence and living-cost evidence are separate. Some applicants qualify for an exemption or different evidence arrangements; check the conditions rather than assuming your nationality or scholarship automatically removes the requirement.

If you use bank statements, check the required holding period and the age of the evidence. If an official financial sponsor supports you, confirm what its letter covers and whether it meets the visa rules. A scholarship that covers tuition but not living costs may leave additional evidence to provide.

Prepare the documents relevant to your case

The application may involve identity documents, financial evidence, English evidence and additional certificates. A tuberculosis test or Academic Technology Approval Scheme certificate is required only where the applicable rules say so. Check translations and make sure names and dates are consistent across documents.

Follow the identity-verification instructions given during the application. Keep copies of the completed form, supporting documents and payment confirmations. Do not book travel on the assumption that a visa decision will arrive on a particular day.

Read the decision and conditions

When a decision is issued, check your digital immigration status or other permission and follow the university's instructions before travelling. Review the course dates, work conditions and any requirements that apply to dependants or changes in study.

For a detailed decision on an unusual situation, contact your university's international student adviser or an appropriately qualified immigration adviser. Use this guide to organise the process; the current official requirements determine what your application needs.

Work from your CAS and current instructions

Before submitting, compare the details on your CAS with your passport and offer. Check the course dates, fees and any payments recorded by the sponsor. If something is wrong, contact the university rather than editing or explaining away an incorrect document yourself. Make a checklist for the evidence that applies to your circumstances, including any required financial, health or academic documents. Keep scans organised and readable. A visa appointment or application payment does not guarantee approval, so distinguish confirmed requirements from travel arrangements you have not yet committed to.

Organise the application around the CAS

The Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies links your visa application to the sponsoring institution and course. When it becomes available, check the personal and course information carefully against your passport and offer. Ask the university to resolve an error before you submit rather than typing a different answer into the visa form and hoping the discrepancy is harmless.

Check what evidence the sponsor used to assess your admission, and which documents the official visa instructions require from you. The university's CAS process and the immigration application are connected but separate. Meeting an academic condition does not automatically establish that financial evidence or another visa requirement has been met.

A practical document sequence

StageActionEvidence to retain
Before the CASMeet the sponsor's conditions and provide requested detailsOffer, fee information and correspondence about outstanding conditions.
After the CASCheck names, course details and recorded paymentsCAS information and any written correction from the sponsor.
Before submittingReview current financial and document instructionsRequired financial evidence, translations and any case-specific documents.
At submissionComplete the official form and identity processSubmitted answers, payment confirmations and appointment details if applicable.
After the decisionRead the permission and access the immigration status recordDecision details and instructions for your individual permission.

Some applicants need additional documents such as an ATAS certificate or tuberculosis test result. The requirement depends on the relevant rules and circumstances. Use the official checklist and sponsor guidance; do not obtain an unrelated document simply because another student needed it.

Check financial evidence as a timeline

Where funds must be held for a specified period, write down the start and end dates and the planned application date. The current GOV.UK money guidance describes a twenty-eight-day holding period and a thirty-one-day relationship between the end of that period and the application date for relevant evidence. Check exemptions and accepted sponsorship or loan evidence separately.

Keep the visa-evidence total separate from everyday affordability. Tuition paid and recorded on the CAS, living-cost evidence, application charges and arrival expenses are different parts of the calculation. Ask the sponsor if a payment is not reflected correctly rather than subtracting it from your evidence without checking the instructions.

Read the decision before making the next assumption

After approval, follow the instructions for accessing and checking your immigration status. Confirm the conditions attached to your permission, including work and study restrictions. If a detail appears incorrect, use the official correction route or your university's advisers promptly. Keep travel plans consistent with the permission actually granted.

Can an academic offer replace a CAS?

An offer is not the CAS required for a Student visa application. Follow the sponsor's process for issuing the CAS after the relevant conditions are met.

Should I use an old checklist from a previous intake?

Use it only to organise early preparation. Check the current government instructions before submitting, especially for evidence amounts, fees and documents that may have changed.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • GOV.UK: Student visa
  • GOV.UK: financial evidence
